findings.summary: The website guard counts any request that names an existing non-website path as a fix. A steward website request citing the site's design doc or README.md would be ranked as a fix.
findings.evidence: xtask/src/site.rs:7 says the site's design is in docs/design/explainer-site.md. The steward's 'code' source is '.' (steward.rs:204-207), so it sees the whole tree and can cite that doc. Under the rule 'true unless some other word satisfies path_exists', a request naming studies/x.json and docs/design/explainer-site.md is a fix. Fix: Add docs/design/explainer-site.md (and any other site-only docs) to WEBSITE_PATHS with a table case, or list this false positive among D181's limits.

findings.summary: A path that ends a sentence keeps its trailing period, so the base-commit lookup misses it. A mixed request can then be classified as website content.
findings.evidence: request_text_touches trims only characters outside alphanumerics and '/._-' (topics.rs:63-64, 334-336), so 'src/lib.rs.' keeps the dot. GitRepo::path_exists then looks up 'HEAD:src/lib.rs.' (athena-git lib.rs:960-962), which does not exist. Fix: In is_website_request, trim trailing '.' from each non-website word before calling path_exists, and add a table case with a path ending a sentence.

findings.summary: Letting the fix flag decide which item keeps a full tier's cap slot means a non-person high feature request can be demoted to normal sooner. That is close to the out-of-scope 'urgent/high caps' item, and the owner was not asked.
findings.evidence: Out of scope lists 'Changing priority levels, urgent/high caps'. The plan concedes this in its risks, and Hestia's root-cause requests are queued High (hestia.rs:1012-1014). The plan lists no open questions. Fix: Keep the documented behavior if preferred, but raise it as an open question for the owner instead of deciding it silently. Alternatively, hand out cap slots from the flag-free order, keeping the second ordering rule small.

findings.summary: `unwrap_or(true)` treats a failed git lookup as an existing path. In the website guard that turns website requests into fixes.
findings.evidence: drain.rs:4353-4354 uses unwrap_or(true) so a git error never invents an open question. In is_website_request, a 'true' for a non-website word makes the request a fix, the opposite of the conservative direction for this rule. Fix: Note the direction in D181, or have the guard's closure use unwrap_or(false) with a comment explaining why it differs from entry_of.

summary: Read the snapshot to check the plan's main claims. plan.rs:767-783 confirms that the sort only sees dependency-free ready items of the best effective priority, so `(!e.fix, e.rung, age)` cannot override priority or dependencies. steward.rs:376-390 and 662-683 confirm the steward channel identifies the steward's open requests. hestia.rs:950-1007 and 1079-1147 confirm `improvement_of`, `cause_jobs`, the private GATE_LINE and `open_gate_request` are as described. drain.rs:4339-4547 confirms `entry_of` is called only from `queue()` and `plan_entry()`, as the wiring plan assumes. The test helpers exist (plan.rs `entry` uses `..PlanEntry::bare`; hestia.rs `put`, `queue_cause_in` and `records`; tests/drain.rs `queue_steward_request` and `complete_request`). `StewardRequest::from_change` takes files from `request_text_touches`, so the criterion 3 fixture texts name the intended paths. Missing paths only add open questions, which drain.rs does not read for ordering. Demonstrations use production entry points and include controls that would fail without the behavior. The dependents list covers the readers I found. Remaining findings are minor: the website path set misses the site's design doc, a path ending a sentence keeps its trailing dot, the cap-slot consequence sits near the out-of-scope caps item, and a failed git lookup counts the path as present, which makes website requests fixes.
